summary: A full VM with preinstalled coding agents and a first-party OpenClaw guide, but no one-click templates, no scheduler and no Hermes material. The $50 Hobby minimum dominates small workloads; a light scraper fits the Free allowances.

routes.what: No Hermes image, template or guide. Create an Ubuntu VM with the SDK or CLI, install Hermes yourself, and turn the idle timeout off so its gateway keeps its connections.
routes.price: About $83/month on Hobby for the 2 vCPU / 4 GiB always-on preset.
routes.disposition: Manual route only; no Hermes material exists, so this is not a recommendation.

routes.what: A first-party guide installs OpenClaw with npm, snapshots it, runs the gateway under systemd and routes a style.dev domain to it. You write the SDK script and supply an OpenAI key.
routes.price: About $83/month on Hobby for the 2 vCPU / 4 GiB always-on preset.
routes.disposition: Guide route; documented and current, but terminal work.

routes.what: Claude Code, Codex and opencode are already in the Ubuntu image. Create a VM, then open a PTY or SSH session and run the agent; the dashboard creates the machine but does not host a chat.

link.title: Run Claude Code in a sandbox

routes.price: $50/month on Hobby at the coding preset (4 vCPU / 8 GiB, 8 h × 20 days), which is the minimum.
routes.disposition: Preinstalled route and a good fit; recommend with the $50 floor and terminal requirement.

routes.what: Build it on the SDK: create an ephemeral VM per run, execute the code, read files back, and delete it. There is no hosted interpreter product or prompt endpoint.
routes.price: About $50/month at 20,000 one-minute runs, which the Hobby minimum covers.
routes.disposition: Backend route only; the product is a VM, not an interpreter.

routes.what: A guide installs Chromium or Chrome, runs it headless or headed with Xvfb and noVNC, and drives it over CDP. The browser is not in the base image.

link.title: Run Chromium and Chrome in a sandbox

routes.price: About $648/month on Hobby at 30,000 ten-minute sessions.
routes.disposition: Guide route; capable but expensive at the shared browser preset.

routes.what: No n8n template. Run the official Docker image on a VM, keep the database and encryption key on its disk, and leave the idle timeout off so webhooks and schedules keep running.
routes.price: About $83/month on Hobby for an always-on 2 vCPU / 4 GiB machine.
routes.disposition: Manual route; no template and no managed database.

routes.what: No Discord or Slack guide. The Telegram bot guide shows the pattern: a systemd service, outbound polling, and no idle timeout so the bot stays connected.

link.title: Run a Telegram bot in a sandbox

routes.price: $50/month on Hobby at the 1 vCPU / 2 GiB always-on preset.
routes.disposition: Manual route; Telegram guide only, Discord and Slack are your own work.

routes.what: Claude Code is preinstalled. Create one VM per developer, add a Linux user, and hand each person a scoped identity token for SSH; the team keeps the account key.
routes.price: About $206/month on Hobby for five 4 vCPU / 8 GiB machines, 8 h × 20 days.
routes.disposition: Preinstalled route; a good fit for per-developer isolation.

routes.what: No scheduler. Trigger the run from your own cron or queue, create an ephemeral VM, scrape, write results to external storage, and let the VM delete itself.
routes.price: $0 on Free at 120 ten-minute runs a month, inside the monthly allowances.
routes.disposition: Manual route, but the cheapest fit: the scraper preset fits the Free allowances.

routes.what: Run your MCP server in a VM and route a style.dev domain to its port; forward auth can gate it. There is no MCP template and no MCP server for controlling Freestyle.
routes.price: $50/month on Hobby at the 1 vCPU / 1 GiB preset, which is the minimum.
routes.disposition: Manual route; a reasonable small always-on endpoint, but the $50 floor is high for one.

picks.for: A coding agent that keeps a full Linux workspace
picks.why: Claude Code and Codex are already installed, pause keeps the session's memory, a live fork lets you try two fixes at once, and the real kernel runs Docker.
picks.watch: The $50 Hobby minimum and the terminal start; there is no region choice.

picks.for: A small team that wants one VM per developer
picks.why: Identities and tokens scope each developer to one VM and one Linux user without sharing the account API key.
picks.watch: No documented team roles or dollar spend cap, and SSO is Enterprise-only.

picks.for: Browser sessions that need a full desktop
picks.why: A full VM runs Chrome headed with Xvfb and noVNC, and a snapshot keeps the installed browser for the next run.
picks.watch: You install Chromium yourself, and allocated CPU is billed for the whole session.

picks.for: OpenClaw on a full VM with memory pause
picks.why: A first-party guide covers the gateway, systemd and a public domain, and pausing keeps the gateway's state.
picks.watch: Terminal-only setup, an OpenAI key, and the $50 minimum.

situationPicks.why: A VM can run indefinitely, pause with memory and resume weeks later; snapshots and forks preserve a long agent run.
situationPicks.watch: Hosts are oversubscribed, and the SLA is Enterprise-only.

situationPicks.why: Docker runs from boot, nested virtual machines work, Pro reaches 32 vCPU / 64 GiB, and a snapshot makes the build environment repeatable.
situationPicks.watch: The company steers sustained CPU work such as kernel builds to other providers.

situationPicks.why: Per-customer slugs, scoped identity tokens and private VPCs are built for multi-tenant products.
situationPicks.watch: No region choice and no documented team roles.

notPicked: hermes-agent: no image, template or guide.
workflow-automation: no n8n template and an always-on machine costs about $83 a month.
chat-bot: no Discord or Slack guide; the Telegram guide is the only pattern.
code-interpreter: no interpreter product, and the $50 minimum is high for short runs.
